$comment: The Superpowers version our workflow has actually been reviewed against. The `sp-version` rule in check-workflow.mjs compares this to the installed version and reports at the severity `workflow-config.mjs` -> VERSION_DRIFT_POLICY assigns to the segment that moved (default: major/minor fail, patch notes). That comparison is the only thing that notices when our prose-enforced dependencies may have stopped holding. Clearing the failure is not editing this file — it is working through references/superpowers-upgrade.md and THEN recording the result here. `gitSha` and `reviewed` are for human traceability; the comparison uses `version` only. The contract is deliberately mechanism-agnostic: this file records what was reviewed, the rule compares it against what is installed, and a difference means the review is owed — no matter how the installed version came to be chosen. Changing how versions are selected therefore does not change anything here.
